prompt: Suppose $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = 4$ and $\lim_{x \to a} g(x) = -2$. Find $\lim_{x \to a} \left[ 3f(x) - g(x) \right]$.
hint: Limits respect constants, sums and differences: you can take the limit of each piece separately.

hints.text: Limits respect constants, sums and differences: you can take the limit of each piece separately.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pretend they are numbers
steps: Near $x = a$, $f(x)$ behaves like $4$ and $g(x)$ behaves like $-2$.
That is $14$. The limit laws say this shortcut is legitimate.
